candidate_relations.reason: Primary sclerosing cholangitis does not produce a 10-cm calcified gallbladder mass invading liver with pulmonary nodules.
Gallbladder cancer is a wording variant of gallbladder carcinoma for this T4N1M1 calcified gallbladder mass.
Metastatic disease names the M1 pulmonary/nodal spread without the gallbladder primary.
Cholangiocarcinoma is a related biliary carcinoma but asserts bile-duct rather than gallbladder origin.
Prior partially calcified gallbladder (porcelain gallbladder) is the predisposing lesion, not the carcinoma itself.
Liver disease is a vague parent of the hepatic invasion/mass.
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma would be a liver-origin tumor rather than gallbladder carcinoma invading segments 4 and 5.
Hepatocellular carcinoma is a hepatocyte tumor, not a calcified gallbladder-wall mass.
The hepatic mass represents direct invasion or metastasis from gallbladder carcinoma, not a separate diagnosis.
There is no colorectal primary; attributing the liver mass to colorectal metastases is a different cancer.
There is no acute inflammatory cholecystitis picture; this is a malignant gallbladder mass.
Metastatic cancer captures T4N1M1 status without gallbladder origin.
